preregistration.title: Independent deeper-project confirmation after product work
preregistration.description: A frozen six-replicate comparison over four new five-module regressions, selected independently of report 031 and run after the v0.3.158 workflow product phase without compiler or instruction tuning.

primary_gate.correctness: Parley hidden-repository success must be 100% and no lower than either baseline.
primary_gate.tokens: Parley median reported total tokens per assigned repository must be no higher than the lower Python/Rust median.
primary_gate.elapsed: Parley median elapsed seconds per assigned repository must be no higher than the lower Python/Rust median.
primary_gate.first_check: Parley first-check repository success rate must be no lower than the higher Python/Rust rate.
primary_gate.verdict: All four conditions must hold for strict efficiency/reliability parity on the independent deeper corpus.

maintainability_gate.root_cause: All 24 Parley assignments must modify exactly the task/language defect file frozen in predeclared_analysis.root_cause_files.
maintainability_gate.caller_compensation: A hidden-correct patch that changes a caller, formatter, cursor, or downstream module in addition to or instead of the owning defect file fails exact-root quality and remains fully reported.
maintainability_gate.overall_verdict: A confirmed maintainable-parity result requires all four primary conditions plus the Parley exact-root condition.

source_protocol.editable_files: Twenty language-specific seeded implementation modules across four repositories.
source_protocol.read_only_files: Twelve language-neutral issue, architecture, and regression artifacts, visibly marked read-only and byte-identical across languages.
source_protocol.public_examples: Protected by the checker and omitted from every agent prompt; diagnosis comes only from editable source and read-only project evidence.
source_protocol.protected_files: Checker, source printer, configuration, prompt, provenance, public/hidden cases, reference fixes, and attempt log are never agent-readable and remain integrity-hashed.

historical_grounding.adapted_mechanism: quoted environment values retain representation markers
Retry-After response evidence is lost before retry scheduling
webhook signatures require access to the exact raw request body
non-unique sort keys duplicate records across page boundaries

interpretation_boundary: The primary result is the within-iteration Parley/Python/Rust comparison under gpt-5.6-sol.
The product implementation, corpus builder, sources, evidence, cases, reference fixes, and root map were validated, committed, and pushed before this protocol or any measured session.
No task mechanism, defect, fixture, or repair was selected from report 031 outcomes; report 031 supplies only the unchanged gate and workload shape.
Historical grounding applies to semantic mechanisms only. Fixtures are deterministic cross-language adaptations and copy no upstream code or tests.
Read-only context is byte-identical across languages; implementation syntax and ordinary standard-library setup remain language-specific.
Root-cause location is a predeclared maintainability judgment separate from hidden-output correctness.
This is an independent six-replicate confirmation, not a pooled extension of iteration 031.
No task, language, or session cell may be selectively rerun, excluded, rewritten, or tuned.
secondary_analysis: Report every session, repository outcome, repair, token count, elapsed time, prompt size, editable-source size, read-only-context size, edit size, changed-file count, integrity result, command event, and file-change event.
Classify every first-check and hidden failure by unrelated repository and independent session before considering any design review.
Report exact-root modification by language, task, and session; show every extra edit without altering hidden correctness.
Report complete token/time distributions, task-level medians, and action shapes; do not replace the primary complete result with a repair-free subset.
Compare with iteration 031 descriptively only; do not pool task cells, gates, or confidence claims across corpora.
preregistration.feature_boundary: Parley is frozen at v0.3.158 after workflow product work. The product phase added CLI workflow contracts and bundled products, not language syntax, compiler semantics, or benchmark instructions.
preregistration.change_rule: No syntax, compiler, grammar, AST, checker, runtime, diagnostic, prompt skill, or benchmark instruction may change from the frozen product checkpoint based on this corpus. Only a semantic signature recurring across independent product or project episodes may enter a separate design review under general usefulness, semantic consistency, maintainability, tests, and documentation.
preregistration.instruction_rule: The proven 1,519-character skill remains byte-for-byte unchanged and is injected once per Parley session. The one allowed instruction-compression experiment is closed.
preregistration.stop_rule: Preserve the complete result without selective reruns. Whether the gates pass or fail, make no same-corpus language, instruction, task, runner, or metric change. Future product or compiler work must be justified independently of benchmark token savings.

source_texts.quoted_environment_project:
to env_kind with token as text giving text:
    if token starts with "dq:" or token starts with "sq:":
        give back "quoted"
    if token is "empty":
        give back "empty"
    give back "raw"

to format_env with key as text, value as text, kind as text giving text:
    give back "key=" + key + "|value=" + value + "|kind=" + kind

include "normalization.par"
include "classification.par"
include "validation.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let key be item 1 of parts
        let token be item 2 of parts
        if (env_supported with token) is no:
            fail "unsupported environment token"
        say (format_env with key, (normalize_env with token), (env_kind with token))

include "std/text"

to normalize_env with token as text giving text:
    if token starts with "sq:":
        give back (without_prefix with token, "sq:")
    if token starts with "dq:":
        give back (without_prefix with token, "dq:")
    if token is "empty":
        give back ""
    give back (without_prefix with token, "raw:")

to env_supported with token as text giving yesno:
    give back token is "empty" or token starts with "dq:" or token starts with "sq:" or token starts with "raw:"
source_texts.stable_pagination_project:
to page_cursor with second as number giving number:
    give back second

to format_page with first as number, second as number, cursor as number giving text:
    give back "first={first}|second={second}|cursor={cursor}"

include "ordering.par"
include "page.par"
include "cursor.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let left_time_input be number from item 1 of parts
        let left_id_input be number from item 2 of parts
        let right_time_input be number from item 3 of parts
        let right_id_input be number from item 4 of parts
        let left_time be value of left_time_input
        let left_id be value of left_id_input
        let right_time be value of right_time_input
        let right_id be value of right_id_input
        let first be (first_item with left_time, left_id, right_time, right_id)
        let second be (second_item with first, left_id, right_id)
        say (format_page with first, second, (page_cursor with second))

to first_item with left_time as number, left_id as number, right_time as number, right_id as number giving number:
    if left_time is less than right_time:
        give back left_id
    if left_time is right_time:
        if left_id is less than right_id:
            give back left_id
        give back right_id
    give back right_id

to second_item with first as number, left_id as number, right_id as number giving number:
    if first is left_id:
        give back right_id
    give back left_id
source_texts.retry_after_precedence_project:
to format_retry with status as text, delay as text, source as text giving text:
    give back "status=" + status + "|delay=" + delay + "|source=" + source

include "retry_policy.par"
include "status.par"
include "source.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let status be item 1 of parts
        let header_delay be item 2 of parts
        let configured_delay be item 3 of parts
        say (format_retry with status, (retry_delay with status, header_delay, configured_delay), (retry_source with status, header_delay, configured_delay))

to retry_delay with status as text, header_delay as text, configured_delay as text giving text:
    if status is not "429":
        give back "0"
    if header_delay is not "none":
        give back header_delay
    if configured_delay is not "none":
        give back configured_delay
    give back "60"

to retry_source with status as text, header_delay as text, configured_delay as text giving text:
    if status is not "429":
        give back "none"
    if header_delay is not "none":
        give back "header"
    if configured_delay is not "none":
        give back "configured"
    give back "default"

to is_throttled with status as text giving yesno:
    give back status is "429"

to captured_body with raw_body as text giving text:
    give back raw_body

to format_webhook with delivery as text, verified as yesno, body as text giving text:
    give back "delivery={delivery}|verified={verified}|body={body}"

include "verification.par"
include "capture.par"
include "normalization.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let delivery be item 1 of parts
        let raw_body be item 2 of parts
        let normalized_body be (normalized_for_application with item 3 of parts)

to normalized_for_application with normalized_body as text giving text:

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. Raw values remove only `raw:`; an explicit empty value stays present and empty. Content after a marker is arbitrary and may contain `=` or marker-like text.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Environment loading flow

`validation` accepts encoded tokens. `classification` records quoted, raw, or empty state. `normalization` owns removal of one outer marker. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair normalization instead of hiding markers in the formatter.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
double-quoted marker is removed once
single-quoted marker is removed once
raw marker is removed without reinterpreting content
empty remains present with an empty value

stable_pagination_project.source_text:
to page_cursor with second as number giving number:
    give back second

to format_page with first as number, second as number, cursor as number giving text:
    give back "first={first}|second={second}|cursor={cursor}"

include "ordering.par"
include "page.par"
include "cursor.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let left_time_input be number from item 1 of parts
        let left_id_input be number from item 2 of parts
        let right_time_input be number from item 3 of parts
        let right_id_input be number from item 4 of parts
        let left_time be value of left_time_input
        let left_id be value of left_id_input
        let right_time be value of right_time_input
        let right_id be value of right_id_input
        let first be (first_item with left_time, left_id, right_time, right_id)
        let second be (second_item with first, left_id, right_id)
        say (format_page with first, second, (page_cursor with second))

to first_item with left_time as number, left_id as number, right_time as number, right_id as number giving number:

        give back left_id
    if left_time is right_time:
        if left_id is less than right_id:
            give back left_id
        give back right_id
    give back right_id

to second_item with first as number, left_id as number, right_id as number giving number:
    if first is left_id:
        give back right_id
    give back left_id

# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.

# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. `validation` accepts encoded tokens. `classification` records quoted, raw, or empty state. `normalization` owns removal of one outer marker. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair normalization instead of hiding markers in the formatter.

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
earlier timestamp sorts first
later timestamp sorts second
equal timestamps use ascending unique ID
cursor is always the ordered second ID

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Retry decision flow

`status` identifies throttling. `retry_policy` owns the selected delay. `source` independently labels the evidence source. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair precedence in the policy instead of changing source labels or presentation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
429 + header + configured -> header delay
429 + no header -> configured delay
429 + neither -> 60-second default
non-429 -> zero delay and no source

# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Retry decision flow

`status` identifies throttling. `retry_policy` owns the selected delay. `source` independently labels the evidence source. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair precedence in the policy instead of changing source labels or presentation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
429 + header + configured -> header delay
429 + no header -> configured delay
429 + neither -> 60-second default
non-429 -> zero delay and no source

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. Raw values remove only `raw:`; an explicit empty value stays present and empty. Content after a marker is arbitrary and may contain `=` or marker-like text.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Environment loading flow

`validation` accepts encoded tokens. `classification` records quoted, raw, or empty state. `normalization` owns removal of one outer marker. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair normalization instead of hiding markers in the formatter.

double-quoted marker is removed once
single-quoted marker is removed once
raw marker is removed without reinterpreting content

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
earlier timestamp sorts first
later timestamp sorts second
equal timestamps use ascending unique ID
cursor is always the ordered second ID

# Webhook signatures fail or validate after body parsing

A signature authenticates the exact captured request bytes. Application normalization may reorder or rewrite the body and is useful only after verification. Compare the provided signature with the raw-body signature; never verify normalized content. The output still exposes the captured body for audit.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Webhook request flow

`capture` owns the immutable raw body. `normalization` prepares application content. `verification` owns signature comparison. `formatting` owns stable audit output. `main` orchestrates. Repair verification instead of bypassing normalization or rewriting audit output.

identical bodies still verify correctly

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Retry decision flow

`status` identifies throttling. `retry_policy` owns the selected delay. `source` independently labels the evidence source. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair precedence in the policy instead of changing source labels or presentation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
429 + header + configured -> header delay
429 + no header -> configured delay
429 + neither -> 60-second default
non-429 -> zero delay and no source

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. Raw values remove only `raw:`; an explicit empty value stays present and empty. Content after a marker is arbitrary and may contain `=` or marker-like text.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Environment loading flow

`validation` accepts encoded tokens. `classification` records quoted, raw, or empty state. `normalization` owns removal of one outer marker. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair normalization instead of hiding markers in the formatter.

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
earlier timestamp sorts first
later timestamp sorts second
equal timestamps use ascending unique ID
cursor is always the ordered second ID

# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. Raw values remove only `raw:`; an explicit empty value stays present and empty. Content after a marker is arbitrary and may contain `=` or marker-like text.

    if token == "empty":

    return "raw"

def normalize_env(token: str) -> str:
    if token.startswith("sq:"):
        return token.removeprefix("sq:")
    if token.startswith("dq:"):
        return token
    if token == "empty":
        return ""
    return token.removeprefix("raw:")

# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.

# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.

retry_after_precedence_project.task_title: Honor server Retry-After before configured backoff

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Retry decision flow

`status` identifies throttling. `retry_policy` owns the selected delay. `source` independently labels the evidence source. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair precedence in the policy instead of changing source labels or presentation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
429 + header + configured -> header delay
429 + no header -> configured delay
429 + neither -> 60-second default
non-429 -> zero delay and no source

stable_pagination_project.task_title: Stabilize pagination ordering with a unique tie-breaker

source_files.cursor.rs: pub fn page_cursor(second: i64) -> i64 { second }

seed_source_files.cursor.rs: pub fn page_cursor(second: i64) -> i64 { second }

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Retry decision flow

`status` identifies throttling. `retry_policy` owns the selected delay. `source` independently labels the evidence source. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair precedence in the policy instead of changing source labels or presentation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
429 + header + configured -> header delay
429 + no header -> configured delay
429 + neither -> 60-second default
non-429 -> zero delay and no source

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. Raw values remove only `raw:`; an explicit empty value stays present and empty. Content after a marker is arbitrary and may contain `=` or marker-like text.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Environment loading flow

`validation` accepts encoded tokens. `classification` records quoted, raw, or empty state. `normalization` owns removal of one outer marker. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair normalization instead of hiding markers in the formatter.

double-quoted marker is removed once
single-quoted marker is removed once
raw marker is removed without reinterpreting content

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
earlier timestamp sorts first
later timestamp sorts second
equal timestamps use ascending unique ID
cursor is always the ordered second ID

# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. # Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.

# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
earlier timestamp sorts first
later timestamp sorts second
equal timestamps use ascending unique ID
cursor is always the ordered second ID

# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.

# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. Raw values remove only `raw:`; an explicit empty value stays present and empty. Content after a marker is arbitrary and may contain `=` or marker-like text.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Environment loading flow

`validation` accepts encoded tokens. `classification` records quoted, raw, or empty state. `normalization` owns removal of one outer marker. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair normalization instead of hiding markers in the formatter.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
double-quoted marker is removed once
single-quoted marker is removed once
raw marker is removed without reinterpreting content
empty remains present with an empty value

    give back left_id

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
earlier timestamp sorts first
later timestamp sorts second
equal timestamps use ascending unique ID
cursor is always the ordered second ID

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Retry decision flow

`status` identifies throttling. `retry_policy` owns the selected delay. `source` independently labels the evidence source. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair precedence in the policy instead of changing source labels or presentation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
429 + header + configured -> header delay
429 + no header -> configured delay
429 + neither -> 60-second default
non-429 -> zero delay and no source

# Webhook signatures fail or validate after body parsing

A signature authenticates the exact captured request bytes. Application normalization may reorder or rewrite the body and is useful only after verification. Compare the provided signature with the raw-body signature; never verify normalized content. The output still exposes the captured body for audit.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Webhook request flow

`capture` owns the immutable raw body. `normalization` prepares application content. `verification` owns signature comparison. `formatting` owns stable audit output. `main` orchestrates. Repair verification instead of bypassing normalization or rewriting audit output.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
raw differs from normalized + raw signature -> verified
raw differs + normalized signature -> rejected
identical bodies still verify correctly
audit body is always the captured raw value

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. Raw values remove only `raw:`; an explicit empty value stays present and empty. Content after a marker is arbitrary and may contain `=` or marker-like text.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Environment loading flow

`validation` accepts encoded tokens. `classification` records quoted, raw, or empty state. `normalization` owns removal of one outer marker. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair normalization instead of hiding markers in the formatter.

double-quoted marker is removed once
single-quoted marker is removed once
raw marker is removed without reinterpreting content
empty remains present with an empty value

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
earlier timestamp sorts first
later timestamp sorts second
equal timestamps use ascending unique ID
cursor is always the ordered second ID

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Retry decision flow

`status` identifies throttling. `retry_policy` owns the selected delay. `source` independently labels the evidence source. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair precedence in the policy instead of changing source labels or presentation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
429 + header + configured -> header delay
429 + no header -> configured delay
429 + neither -> 60-second default
non-429 -> zero delay and no source

stable_pagination_project.task_title: Stabilize pagination ordering with a unique tie-breaker

source_files.cursor.rs: pub fn page_cursor(second: i64) -> i64 { second }

seed_source_files.cursor.rs: pub fn page_cursor(second: i64) -> i64 { second }

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.

later timestamp sorts second
equal timestamps use ascending unique ID

retry_after_precedence_project.task_title: Honor server Retry-After before configured backoff

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Retry decision flow

`status` identifies throttling. `retry_policy` owns the selected delay. `source` independently labels the evidence source. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair precedence in the policy instead of changing source labels or presentation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
429 + header + configured -> header delay
429 + no header -> configured delay
429 + neither -> 60-second default
non-429 -> zero delay and no source

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. Raw values remove only `raw:`; an explicit empty value stays present and empty. Content after a marker is arbitrary and may contain `=` or marker-like text.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Environment loading flow

`validation` accepts encoded tokens. `classification` records quoted, raw, or empty state. `normalization` owns removal of one outer marker. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair normalization instead of hiding markers in the formatter.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
double-quoted marker is removed once
single-quoted marker is removed once
raw marker is removed without reinterpreting content
empty remains present with an empty value

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Retry decision flow

`status` identifies throttling. `retry_policy` owns the selected delay. `source` independently labels the evidence source. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` orchestrates. Repair precedence in the policy instead of changing source labels or presentation.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
429 + header + configured -> header delay
429 + no header -> configured delay
429 + neither -> 60-second default
non-429 -> zero delay and no source

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.
context_source_files.architecture/flow.md:
# Pagination flow

`ordering` owns the stable first item. `page` derives the second item. `cursor` advances from that second item. `formatting` owns stable output. `main` parses and orchestrates. Repair ordering rather than compensating in cursor or presentation code.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
earlier timestamp sorts first
later timestamp sorts second
equal timestamps use ascending unique ID
cursor is always the ordered second ID

# Adjacent pages duplicate items when timestamps tie

Pagination orders records by creation time, but timestamps are not unique. A stable total order must use ascending creation time and then ascending unique ID. The page cursor is the second item's ID after ordering. Without the ID tie-breaker, equal-time records can swap and appear twice across page boundaries.

# Quoted environment values keep their quote marker

The environment loader represents matching double and single quotes as `dq:` and `sq:` markers. Both markers are syntax and must be removed exactly once. Raw values remove only `raw:`; an explicit empty value stays present and empty. Content after a marker is arbitrary and may contain `=` or marker-like text.

# Client ignores Retry-After while throttled

For HTTP 429, a server-provided Retry-After delay is authoritative and must override configured backoff. Configured backoff is used only when the header is absent; otherwise use the 60-second default. Non-429 responses are not scheduled for retry by this policy.
